title: Asuman Ozdaglar — Strategic Form Games and Nash Equilibrium, July 15, 2013
use: Author-hosted university teaching chapter for finite normal-form and mixed strategies, product probabilities, unilateral-deviation inequalities, support characterization and the finite mixed Nash existence statement.
verification: Retrieved the full 13-page PDF and inspected sections 2, 3, 3.1 and 4.1, PDF pages 2–7 (printed pages 1–6). Read pure/mixed equilibrium definitions, Propositions 1 and 2 including the support argument, and Theorem 1. The source explicitly states that its fixed-point existence proofs are omitted; the manuscript likewise invokes the fixed-point theorem and gives only an honest route, while independently proving the finite support test. The original 3-by-2 example and all exercises are newly constructed, not copied source problems. Continuous-action existence and the later game classes are not claimed as covered.

title: Muhamet Yildiz — MIT 14.12 Chapter 4: Dominance, 2012 notes hosted with the Fall 2025 course
use: Primary university source for pure and mixed strict domination, best responses to beliefs, weak dominance and the zero-probability/tie qualification.
verification: Retrieved the full 15-page PDF and read sections 4.1–4.2, PDF pages 1–6 (printed pages 51–56). Definitions and belief comparisons were inspected directly. The original weak-deletion table, deletion orders and mixture-dominance calculations are independently derived in the manuscript. Author provenance was checked on https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/14-12-economic-applications-of-game-theory-fall-2025/lists/lecture-notes/: MIT explicitly identifies these as notes created by Muhamet Yildiz for the 2012 class. The 2025 course instructor is not represented as their author. No universal weak-deletion or order-independence theorem is asserted.

title: Muhamet Yildiz — MIT 14.12 Chapter 3: Representation of Games, 2012 notes hosted with the Fall 2025 course
use: Primary university source for extensive histories, information sets, chance moves, complete contingent strategies, normal-form representation and mixed strategies.
verification: Retrieved the full 23-page PDF and inspected sections 3.1.3–3.1.4, 3.2 and the normal-form/mixed definitions of 3.3: information sets on PDF pages 6–8, chance/common-knowledge discussion on pages 8–9, strategies on pages 10–11, normal form on pages 12–13 and mixed definitions around page 16. These support the constraints that an information set has one player and common actions and that a strategy assigns one action there, including unreached contingencies. The complete-versus-perfect-information distinction and the original observed/hidden coordination exercise are stated explicitly. MIT's official lecture-notes listing verifies Yildiz's 2012 authorship. No behavioral/mixed-strategy equivalence theorem is claimed or used.

title: Muhamet Yildiz — MIT 14.12 Chapter 9: Backward Induction, 2012 notes hosted with the Fall 2025 course
use: Primary university method source for backward induction in finite perfect-information trees, optimal continuation selection and the role of finite-horizon assumptions.
verification: Retrieved the 23-page PDF and inspected sections 9.1–9.2, PDF pages 1–6 (printed pages 131–136), including the finite-node procedure and Proposition 9.1 optimality argument. The manuscript supplies its own induction over solved child continuations, retains ties and specifies full off-path plans in an original entry/commitment tree. The source's later applications and infinite-horizon material were not used as evidence of complete coverage. MIT's official lecture-notes listing verifies Yildiz's 2012 authorship.

title: Muhamet Yildiz — MIT 14.12 Chapter 11: Subgame-Perfect Nash Equilibrium, 2012 notes hosted with the Fall 2025 course
use: Primary university source for subgame information-set closure, equilibrium in all subgames, off-path incentives and limits of subgame perfection in imperfect-information games.
verification: Retrieved the full 27-page PDF and inspected section 11.1, PDF pages 1–6 (printed pages 173–178), including definitions, examples of subgames and the warning that SPNE need not fully formalize sequential rationality when information sets prevent proper subgames. The original entry normal form, noncredible threat and commitment mechanism are independently computed. No general one-shot-deviation theorem, bargaining theorem or sequential-equilibrium characterization is claimed here. MIT's official lecture-notes listing verifies Yildiz's 2012 authorship; the later host-course date is not a new authorship claim.
